correctness.rationale: Necessity: a uniquely defining formula over computable constant parameters yields a computable 1−distance function and a terminating effective dense-point search. In a finite relational structure every singleton stabilizer orbit is first-order parameter-definable by an existential finite diagram, establishing dcl_M(S)=Fix(G_S). Sufficiency: a finite list of all nontrivial stabilizer automorphisms acts over private rational intervals on initial segments of irrational noncomputable relative measure. Transported names retain the exact standard decidable diagram, while a moved constant would compute a private noncomputable measure if it possessed a standard-coordinate fast name. This establishes both directions and all edge cases, including rigid and singleton structures; finite enumeration is auxiliary, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact possible recoverable-constant sets form a natural Galois closure system, answering a sharply formulated classification question left open by binary nonawareness examples. It identifies a forbidden co-singleton cardinality for every finite pure set, distinguishes rigid versus nonrigid finite structures, and resolves every subset (not merely one size or an arbitrary parameter slice). The same construction realizes all cases within one computable isomorphism type, isolating the external-versus-intrinsic effective asymmetry. This structural classification is motivated independently of the small finite checker.
